title: What Do News Aggregators Do? Evidence from Google News in Spain and Germany
eligible_reason: Not staggered. Spain: Google News shutdown on a single date (afterSP = 1 after Dec 16, 2014) for Spanish outlets vs. French or Italian outlets. Germany: a single two-week opt-out window of VG Media outlets (DuringGermany). Advertising: newspapers vs. services after Dec 16, 2014. All regressions also include country/group-specific quadratic time trends (datespain, datespain_2, ...), heterogeneity interactions, and the shipped data are generated from fitted values plus noise.
design_notes: SWdofile_Spain.do: xi: reg ldvisits Spain afterSP afterSPinSP datefrance datespain datefrance_2 datespain_2 i.date i.site if exercise1==1, cluster(site). SWdofile_Germany.do: areg ldvisits Germany DuringGermany DuringGerinGer ... date trends i.date, a(site). Advertising_dofile.do: areg lnrevenue treatment post161214 treatmentpost datetreat datetreatsq ... i.date, a(site_marca_nivel). Synthetic-control exercise files also shipped.
data_files_note: README: 'The data posted is generated from regression equations in the paper' - outcomes are predicted values from the published regressions, rescaled by lambda and perturbed with N(0,1) noise.
data_provenance_note: Outcomes generated from fitted regression values times a factor plus normal noise (README steps 1-6).
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available; screened from README, code and OpenAlex abstract. Two separate single-date events (Spain Dec 2014, Germany Oct-Nov 2014) are estimated in separate samples, so neither design has two adoption cohorts. Verified in shipped data: all 59 Spanish sites switch afterSPinSP on 2014-12-17; DuringGermany = 1 from 2014-10-23 to 2014-11-05 for all German outlets.
